archivalTracks.trackName: Birds of Earth & Morning Dawn Chorus
archivalTracks.description: Songbirds of the temperate forest, including Wood Thrush, American Robin, Keel-billed Toucan, and nightingale calls recorded in pristine natural sanctuaries.
archivalTracks.nasaSource: Cornell Lab of Ornithology & NASA Voyager Audio Curation

archivalTracks.description: Deep ocean vocalizations of Megaptera novaeangliae recorded by Dr. Roger Payne, echoing through the deep sound channel (SOFAR layer).
archivalTracks.nasaSource: New York Zoological Society & NASA Voyager Science Team

archivalTracks.description: Continuous rhythmic breakers on rocky headlands and tropical sandy beaches, gentle throughfall canopy rain, and mountain gale winds.
archivalTracks.nasaSource: NASA Atmospheric & Oceanic Field Sound Archive

archivalTracks.description: Low-frequency geothermal rumblings, bubbling thermal mud pots, and distant rolling atmospheric lightning discharges.
archivalTracks.nasaSource: USGS / NASA Earth Surface Acoustic Surveys

archivalTracks.description: Intimate human piano memory evoking friendship, memory, and the longing of Eli across interstellar space.
archivalTracks.nasaSource: Voyager Golden Record Music of Earth Collection

integratedSystemMetrics.biosphereCanopyIndex: NASA GEDI L4B Mean Canopy Height (rh100 = 34.8m)
integratedSystemMetrics.hydrosphereCurrentSpeed: NASA ECCO V4r4 Mean Surface Velocity (0.42 m/s)
integratedSystemMetrics.atmospherePressureStability: NASA MERRA-2 Mean Global Sea Level Pressure (1013.25 hPa)

scientificTransparency.dataOrigin: Authentic acoustic and musical tracks curated by NASA's Voyager Golden Record Committee chaired by Carl Sagan, encoded on gold-plated copper phonograph records aboard Voyager 1 and 2, combined with integrated Earth system metrics.
scientificTransparency.disclaimer: This represents the permanent interstellar time capsule launched by NASA to represent life and sounds on planet Earth to the cosmos.
